drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 77-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.51, creatinine 0.73-0.78, hemoglobin 13.7-13.8, platelets 312-320, sodium 130-133, wbc 7.7-8.3; vitals dbp 69-72, heart_rate 71-76, map 86-89, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 118-124, spo2 95-97, temp 36.7-37
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Fluid restriction 1.2 L/day; Sodium chloride 1 g PO TID
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.74-0.77, hemoglobin 13.6-13.8, platelets 313-323, sodium 133-135, wbc 7.9-8.3; vitals dbp 67-72, heart_rate 72-76, map 85-87, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 13-15, sbp 117-123, spo2 96, temp 36.7-37
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 77-year-old female, length of stay 5 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
